result.topic_en: Dedekind defines rational number classes (a,r) = [a]+r (residue classes of rationals modulo a rational module), computes their intersection, sum and product, proves commutativity and associativity of the product, and determines all classes (b,s) acting as identity on a given class (a,r).
result.transcription:
Rationale Zahlclassen
Sind $a$, $r$ rationale Zahlen, so soll unter $(a,r)$ das System aller Zahlen $ax+r$ verstanden werden, wo $x$ alle ganzen rationalen Zahlen durchläuft, also $(a,r) = [a]+r$.

Welche Zahlen haben $(a,r)$, $(b,s)$ gemeinsam? $ax+r = by+s$ giebt $r-s = -ax+by$, also
Bedingung $[r-s, a, b] = [a,b]$, d.h. $r \equiv s \pmod{[a,b]}$
Setzt man $[\partial] = [a,b]$; [-ist $\partial = ax_0+by_0$, $ax+by = \partial z = ax_0 z + by_0 z$;
$a(x-zx_0) = b(zy_0-y) = \frac{ab}{\partial}z'$; $x = zx_0+\frac{b}{\partial}z'$; $y = zy_0 - \frac{a}{\partial}z'$-]
[-$ax+r$-]
$ax_0+r = by_0+s = t$; $ax+r = by+s$
$a(x-x_0) = b(y-y_0)$; $x-x_0 = \frac{b}{\partial}z$, $y-y_0 = \frac{a}{\partial}z$
$x = x_0+\frac{b}{\partial}z$; $y = y_0+\frac{a}{\partial}z$
$ax+r = ax_0+r+\frac{ab}{\partial}z = t+\frac{ab}{\partial}z = by+r$
[-Gemeinheit $(a,r)$ $(b,r)$-] Durchschnitt $(a,r)\curlyvee(b,s) = (\frac{ab}{\partial}, t)$; $\curlyvee$ Zeichen für Durchschnitt[?].

$(a,r)\pm(b,s) = (\partial, r\pm s)$; besteht aus allen Zahlen $ax+r\pm by\pm s = \partial z+(r\pm s)$
Jedes Product aus einer Zahl in $(a,r)$ und einer Zahl in $(b,s)$ ist
$= (ax+r)(by+s) = abxy+asx+bry+rs \equiv rs \pmod{[ab, as, br]}$
Wir definiren
[-...-] $(a,r)(b,s) = ([ab,as,br], rs) = (b,s)(a,r)$ Commutativ.

also ist
$\{(a,r)(b,s)\}(c,t) = ([ab,as,br],rs)(c,t) = (h,k)(c,t) = ([hc,ht,ck],kt]$
$[hc,ht,ck] = [abc, acs, bcr, abt, ast, brt, crs]$; $kt = rst$
Also Associativ.
{+Aus $(a,r)(b,r) = (h,k)$ folgt immer $[a,r][b,s] = [h,k]$+}

$(a,r) = (b,s)$ ist gleichbedeutend mit $a = \pm b$; $r \equiv s \pmod{a}$

$(a,r)$ gegeben; gesucht alle $(b,s)$, die $(a,r)(b,s) = (a,r)$ geben
$[ab, as, br] = [a]$; $rs \equiv r \pmod{a}$
also $[b, s, \frac{br}{a}] = [1]$; es sei $[1, \frac{r}{a}] = \frac{1}{a_0}$; $[a,r] = \frac{a}{a_0}$; dann $[\frac{b}{a_0}, s] = 1$
$b = ha_0$; $[h,s] = 1$; $r(s-1) = ak$
$a(s-1) = a(s-1)$ | $\frac{a}{a_0}(s-1) = au$; $s-1 = a_0 u$
$(b,s) = (ha_0, 1+ka_0)$, wo $h, k$ ganz und $\frac{1}{a_0} = [1, \frac{r}{a}]$ und $[h, 1+ka_0] = [1]$
$(h_1a_0, 1+k_1a_0)(h_2a_0, 1+k_2a_0) = ([h_1h_2a_0^2, h_1a_0s_2, h_2a_0s_1], s_1s_2)$
$[\ \ ] = a_0[h_1h_2a_0, h_1s_2, h_2s_1] = a_0[h_1, h_2]$, weil $[h_1a_0, s_1] = [h_2a_0, s_2] = [1]$
